#38448. QPR should proposal January loan exit for 23-year-old ahead of injury comeback: Opinion

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (575 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

QPR should proposal January loan exit for 23-year-old ahead of injury comeback: Opinion

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (575 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • QPR didn’t touch their attacking ranks in the summer transfer window.
  • Despite this, Julien Stephan has a deep group of forwards to choose from.
  • Recent findings suggest that it can lead to reduced opportunities for some players though, and Alfie Lloyd has met that fate with Rayan Kolli reintegrated and Rumarn Burrell returning from injury.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

QPR didn’t touch their attacking ranks in the summer transfer window. Of their six signings, two were goalkeepers, three were full-backs, and one was a central midfielder.

Despite this, Julien Stephan has a deep group of forwards to choose from. Injuries have tested the Frenchman’s options at Loftus Road, but with as many as 11 players capable of operating in attacking roles, the Hoops have good depth and versatility to work with.

Recent findings suggest that it can lead to reduced opportunities for some players though, and Alfie Lloyd has met that fate with Rayan Kolli reintegrated and Rumarn Burrell returning from injury. Lloyd is sidelined himself with a hamstring concern set to keep him out until 2027, but when January rolls around, a loan exit could be best for the 23-year-old.

Sources indicate that lloyd has played 40 times for the QPR first team since joining the club as a youngster in 2021. He progressed with the development squad and spent time out on loan at Eastleigh before becoming a more regular feature on the senior scene.

Sources indicate that but, after signing the likes of Burrell and Richard Kone in the summer of 2025, Lloyd was loaned out. A stint at Leyton Orient didn’t have much fruit to bear, but he had a better spell at Lincoln City over the second half of the season.

It has been revealed that at Sincil Bank, Lloyd offered a similar presence to the one he has with the Hoops. He’s a hard-working and powerful forward who is effective at running into channels, drifting across the front three and stretching the defence. It means he can really disrupt games off the bench, be it as a striker or winger.

But, with Burrell and Kone fit, Kolli back in the senior squad and Justin Obikwu lurking, opportunities at striker will be limited for Lloyd. The same goes for the left-hand side, as the fit-again Ilias Chair joins Koki Saito and Paul Smyth as options on that flank.

Industry observers note that aged 23, Lloyd needs to be playing regularly, and not for the development squad. A loan back down to League One level would give the forward the game time he needs to grow.

Depth is key in a Championship play-off push, and there’s no reason why QPR can’t target such heights.

At striker and on both flanks, players returning from injuries mean that the R’s have no shortage of options. Cover is essential, of course, but it could be that the likes of Lloyd and Obikwu are left on the outskirts.

Industry observers note that once Lloyd returns, he will be eager to get back into the action. He has a better chance of doing so away from Loftus Road and will have no shortage of admirers eager to bring him in.

Breaking: Nice vs. Paris Saint-Germain - prediction, team news, lineups

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (679 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Seye Omidiora | 19 Nov 2026 21:07.
  • Two of Ligue 1's form sides meet at Allianz Riviera this weekend as Nice seek to end Paris Saint-Germain's winning streak in Saturday's matchday-11 tussle.
  • Luis Enrique's men are chasing an eighth consecutive league victory and a 12th straight win across all competitions, while the Eaglets aim to build on a run that yielded nine points from nine before the hiatus.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 19 Nov 2026 21:07.

Two of Ligue 1's form sides meet at Allianz Riviera this weekend as Nice seek to end Paris Saint-Germain's winning streak in Saturday's matchday-11 tussle.

Luis Enrique's men are chasing an eighth consecutive league victory and a 12th straight win across all competitions, while the Eaglets aim to build on a run that yielded nine points from nine before the hiatus.

Something has shifted for Olivier Pantaloni's men since they failed to defeat 10-man Lyon last month, with Les Aiglons embarking on their longest Ligue 1 winning streak of 2026.

Indeed, Nice have not won as many consecutive matches since October 2025, a sequence that proved the highlight for supporters during a campaign in which interim boss Claude Puel eventually steered Le Gym to safety following a 16th-placed finish.

Pantaloni's impressive start has helped the Eaglets put the 2025-26 campaign behind them, with five victories and two draws from their opening 10 matches leaving them sixth in the standings.

All five of Les Aiglons' victories have come in their last six games, underlining their improvement in performances and results after a four-match winless start that produced two draws.

Only PSG have collected more than Nice's 15 points across the last six gameweeks, but Pantaloni's team now seek to halt the capital club's remarkable winning run.

The Parisians failed to win any of their opening three matches of the 2026-27 season, losing once and drawing twice, but the reigning French and European champions have since turned the screw to lead the table.

Lille and Paris FC remain two and three points behind Enrique's men respectively, underlining how well those early-season high-flyers have kept pace with PSG's surge.

Enrique's side now travel to Allianz Riviera aiming to end the hosts' unbeaten home run, with Nice having collected 11 points from a possible 15 in front of their supporters.

Only Lyon, Paris and Rennes have earned more home points this season, with 13 apiece, underlining the significance of PSG's visit on Saturday.

Conversely, the capital club are also unbeaten on their travels, collecting 14 points from a possible 18 and scoring a prolific 15 goals across six away matches, six more than their nearest challengers Marseille, Toulouse and Strasbourg.

The travelling supporters will therefore hope that their side's attacking proficiency serves them well at a ground where PSG have not lost since 2022, recording three victories during that period.

Paris Saint-Germain Ligue 1 form:.

Paris Saint-Germain form (all competitions):.

Nice have several absentees ahead of Saturday's clash with PSG: Antoine Mendy (knee), Moise Bombito (leg), Laurent Abergel (knee) and Mohamed Abdelmonem (muscle) are all unlikely to feature.

Nonetheless, the Eaglets have several match-winners capable of troubling the defending Ligue 1 champions, with leading scorer Elye Wahi aiming to add to his six goals and two assists.

Three of Sofiane Diop's five direct goal involvements have come across the last three Ligue 1 matches, while Jonathan Clauss has scored or assisted in four of his last five top-flight appearances.

PSG may be the division's leading scorers, but Ferran Torres's four goals and Achraf Hakimi's three stand out among Enrique's attacking returns.

Marquinhos's three league goals are particularly notable, as are Ilya Zabarnyi's two in five appearances, placing the latter level with Mika Godts and Senny Mayulu.

However, Marquinhos is doubtful for Saturday due to a thigh injury, alongside Nuno Mendes, Ousmane Dembele, Maghnes Akliouche (calf), Desire Doue (hamstring) and Dro Fernandez (muscle), while Khvicha Kvaratskhelia (knee) remains a long-term absentee.

Diouf; Seidu, Ndayishimiye, Mandza; Clauss, Witsel, Boudaoui, Nkounkou; Diop, Amoura; Wahi.

Paris Saint-Germain possible starting lineup:.

Safonov; Hakimi, Zabarnyi, Pacho, Hernandez; Neves, Vitinha, Ruiz; Akliouche, Torres, Godts.

Nice's resurgence deserves considerable respect, but their defensive absences present an unwelcome complication against the division's most productive attack.

PSG have not lost at Allianz Riviera since 2022 and should have enough midfield control and attacking variety to extend their winning sequence without requiring a spectacular performance.

Joao Pedro double and Caicedo stunner give Chelsea win over AC Milan

📅 08 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 16 min read (3193 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~16 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that chelsea cruised to victory over Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan in Jakarta, Indonesia, on Saturday.
  • The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Moises Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.
  • The west London side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that chelsea cruised to victory over Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan in Jakarta, Indonesia, on Saturday. Goals from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to their second win on their Far East tour.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Moises Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

The west London side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

MOISÉS CAICEDO THAT IS INCREDIBLE 🤯 pic.twitter.com/C6CEcUG1sE.

Chelsea had further chances to extend their lead in a dominant second-half performance but were unable to add to their three goals.

Chelsea conclude their tour of the Far East with a game against Johor Darul Ta’zim on Sunday in Malaysia before returning home.

Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge before beginning their Premier League campaign at Fulham.

AC Milan take on Amorim’s former club Manchester United next Saturday before they kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

Chelsea managed to lure Austin MacPhee to take care of their set-pieces and today Chelsea scored two goals from corners. Here is a snippet of Mike McGrath’s piece on MacPhee’s arrival at Chelsea:.

He is among the new breed of coaches who are rock stars in their own right, taking centre-stage since rules were changed so that only one person is allowed in the technical area at a time. For MacPhee to get closer to the players for a set-piece, it will mean Xabi Alonso taking a step back onto the bench.

It has been an incredible rise for MacPhee, 46, who was working on Michael O’Neill’s staff with Northern Ireland 10 years ago this summer, helping them reach the knockout stages of the European Championship.

Chelsea take on Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia tomorrow before returning to the UK. Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad before taking on Fulham on the opening weekend of the new season.

AC Milan will play Manchester United next weekend and then kick off their Serie A campaign against Torino.

Possession: Chelsea 50%-50% AC MilanShots: 18-5Shots on target: 8-0Corners: 7-2.

In a recent development, the final whistle is blown in Jakarta and Chelsea have cruised to a 3-0 win over AC Milan. Goals from Caicedo and a double from Pedro either side of half-time have led Xabi Alonso’s side to the victory. They have one more game out in the Far East before returning home to the UK.

What a performance! 👏 pic.twitter.com/GcUZXwXbRj.

Ramos is picked out after making a run into the Chelsea box and is denied by Sanchez. However, the offside flag has gone up anyway against Ramos. AC Milan have barely threatened the Chelsea goal in this second half.

A late change for Chelsea as Sarr replaces Fofana.

There will be five added minutes.

Chelsea are seeking their fourth goal as Quenda strikes a shot powerfully from just outside the box but it goes narrowly wide. Xabi Alonso’s side have dominated this second half.

Estevao has the chance to score moments after coming on after good work from the Brazilian down Chelsea’s right but is denied by a good save from Torriani.

Chelsea make a triple changes as Estevao, Mudryk and Watson come on. Mudryk made his return after his doping ban against Juventus during the week.

Chelsea hit the frame of the goal once more. Jackson gets the better of Vladimirov down Chelsea’s left and moves into the AC Milan penalty area. Jackson opens up his body as if he is going to curl his shot into the far corner but instead shoots towards the near corner, with his effort coming off the post.

Ricci goes for an audacious strike with the outside of his right foot from outside the box but his effort misses the target.

Palmer was deep in conversation with his boss Alonso during that water break.

Sources indicate that chelsea made a substitution during that break as Anselmino comes on for Hato. Thus far, Chelsea have made three changes in this game and Alonso did confirm before the game that some players should be able to go the full 90 this far into pre-season.

Time for the second half water break.

Chelsea hit the post. Quenda receives the ball on the right side of the penalty area and quickly moves the ball onto his right foot. The 19-year-old then smashes a shot towards goal and the ball flies into the outside of the post. Quenda struck that with some venom.

Palmer has a chance to get Chelsea’s fourth from the left side of the box but AC Milan keeper Torriani makes the save down to his left.

AC Milan have offered very little going forward since the break and Sanchez has not been troubled in the Chelsea goal.

AC Milan have a good chance to get a goal back. Musah finds space on the right side of the box and cuts it back towards the penalty spot. He picks out Nkunku but the former Chelsea man wastes the opportunity.

It has been revealed that palestra is found with a cross from the right to the far post. Palestra takes a touch but his shot goes into the side netting.

Ruben Amorim is demanding a free-kick just outside the Chelsea box but the referee does not agree. Replays show that AC Milan probably should have been given the free-kick as it was a foul by Fofana on Ramos. Both players went down but are back to their feet.

Xabi Alonso is going to make his first two changes of the game as Jackson and Quenda replace Welbeck and Neto.

Chelsea have their third and their upcoming set-piece coach Austin MacPhee will be delighted with that one. Lavia plays a flat delivery from a corner out on the left to Caicedo on the edge of the box. Caicedo hits it first time on the volley with the outside of his right foot and picks out the bottom right corner with perfection.

Industry observers note that chelsea go 2-0 up not even a minute into the second half. Neto, on the right side of the box, cuts onto his preferred left foot and crosses to the far post. Pedro gets on the end of it and, despite the Milan keeper getting a touch on the shot, the ball ends up in the far corner.

AC Milan have made a raft of changes at the break, which includes their new record signing Ramos, who has joined from PSG this summer. Former Chelsea man Nkunku is also on. Milan were back out from the dressing rooms a fair bit earlier than Chelsea were. It is rather farcical how long Chelsea took to re-emerge for the second half and they just saunter out as if nothing is up. Why on earth did the officials just allow Chelsea to take over 20 minutes for half-time?

Nearly 25 minutes after the first half concluded, we are finally back under way in Jakarta.

Possession: Chelsea 58%-42% AC MilanShots: 6-4Shots on target: 3-0Corners: 4-2.

The first half in Jakarta is brought an end and Chelsea take a 1-0 lead into the break courtesy of Pedro’s goal on the stroke of half-time.

According to recent reports, 90 seconds into added time at the end of this first half, we have the first goal in Jakarta. Caicedo’s delivery from the right picks out Pedro, who has a free header inside the six-yard box and makes no mistake, picking out the corner. Pedro really should not have been afforded so much space in the six-yard box.

Palestra makes a run in behind the AC Milan defence and is found but De Winter gets back to put it behind for a corner...

Due to the water break, there will be three additional minutes at the end of this first half.

It has been revealed that the first booking of the game goes the way of AC Milan as Pavlovic clears out Palestra. A deserved booking.

In a recent development, neto and Pedro exchange a good one-two down Chelsea’s right to put the former racing down the right wing. Neto then tries to find Welbeck in the centre of the box but it is just behind him.

In a recent development, then, moments later, Pedro spurns a great chance for Chelsea. Palestra’s cross from the left is just out of Palmer’s reach but falls straight to Pedro, who blazes over from 12 yards out. He was leaning back and should really be hitting the target.

Sources indicate that the space opens up for Palmer to take on a shot from range but his effort is blocked by De Winter. Palmer has not managed to have that much of an effect on this game thus far.

Recent findings suggest that pavlovic drives forward from his defensive position through the Chelsea half. He gets all the way to the Chelsea box before shooting but he looked to lack conviction, firing off target.

Industry observers note that we will pause for a drinks break, which unfortunately we became accustomed to during the World Cup. Palmer takes the chance to take a seat on the bench whilst taking on some fluids.

Neto takes a first-time shot from outside the box and looks to curl it into the far corner, forcing Torriani into a decent save diving down to his right.

That is good one-vs-one defending from Achemapong. Estupinan plays the ball into the path of Leao, who drives through the Chelsea half down AC Milan’s left. As Leao approaches the Chelsea box, Leao attempts to push it past Acheampong but the young Chelsea defender times his sliding challenge to perfection and puts it behind for a corner. Sanchez punches it out to the edge of the box, where Comotto takes it on his chest before volleying towards goal. The ball goes behind for another corner, which Chelsea just about scramble away.

In a recent development, chelsea hit the post. Palestra drives forward for Chelsea down their left before the ball falls to Welbeck on the left side of the box. Welbeck’s effort hits the outside of the post. AC Milan keeper Torriani appeared though to always have it covered.

Recent findings suggest that chelsea gift the ball away inside their own half and Leao drives forward. The Portuguese forward moves into the Chelsea penalty area before getting his shot away but his effort is blocked.

According to recent reports, A big, big chance for Chelsea to take the lead. A long ball is played forward in behind the AC Milan defence and Pedro gets the better of De Winter inside the Milan penalty area. It is then a one-on-one chance with Torriani but Pedro hits it straight at the Milan goalkeeper. Torriani should have come to claim that long ball and then Pedro should probably have buried that opportunity.

Recent findings suggest that chelsea win their third corner of the game as Palmer’s cross from the right takes a couple of deflections off AC Milan defender. Captain Caicedo has trotted over to take it out on the left. He sends it into a good area but a foul on the AC Milan keeper Torriani is given against Pedro.

Industry observers note that neto clips a free-kick into the AC Milan penalty area, which is chested down by Pedro. The Brazilian holds the ball up well inside the box before winning a corner. Chelsea play it short and Palmer crosses to the back post, where Palestra wins Chelsea another corner, this time out on the left.

Caicedo’s inswinging delivery is headed away at the front post.

Palestra, who has joined Chelsea this summer from Atalanta, is proving his versatility today; he has mostly operated for Chelsea at right-back so far this pre-season but he is starting at left-back in this game.

Camarda is played in behind the Chelsea defence and tries to get the better of Fofana inside the Chelsea penalty area but the ball just runs out of play across the byline before Camarda can square the ball.

We are under way in Jakarta, Indonesia, in Chelsea’s penultimate game over in the Far East. Before the game started, a huge AC Milan tifo was unveiled at one end of the ground.

In a recent development, it is 7pm in Jakarta yet the temperature is still up at 29 degrees with the humidity at nearly 70%. These conditions will be a proper test for both sides.

The teams emerge from the tunnel and we are just moments away from kick-off in Indonesia.

The trophies won by Franco Baresi, who has died at the age of 66, are their own monument to the AC Milan and Italy defender’s greatness. Six times a Serie A champion, five as captain, three European Cup-winning campaigns, 10 other winners’ medals and the distinction of being a member of Italy squads that finished in first, second and third places at World Cup tournaments demonstrate that his career, in a significantly more meritocratic era, stand alongside the giants even if the bias towards attacking virtuosos denied him the Ballon d’Or his talent deserved.

In a recent development, yet they do not tell us why the grief, so tangible in Milan and beyond today, transcends tribal rivalry. It would be unfair to say that he transformed the art of Italian defending. Gaetano Scirea, the elegant Juventus sweeper who kept the 21-year-old Baresi confined to the bench when Italy won their third World Cup in 1982, had a surplus of natural ability, composure and intelligence. He did not need the raw-elbowed brutality of Claudio Gentile, heir to generations of Italian defenders influenced by the post-war influx of players brought up in the traditions of Argentina and Uruguay.

INS:Marco Palestra ⇠ Atalanta, £42mGeovany Quenda ⇠ Sporting, £42mMorgan Rogers ⇠ Aston Villa, £117mMaxence Lacroix ⇠ Crystal Palace, £51mDanny Welbeck ⇠ Brighton, UndisclosedJordan Henderson ⇠ Brentford, FreeValentin Barco ⇠ Strasbourg, Undisclosed.

OUTS:Andrey Santos ⇢ Manchester United, £50mMarc Cucurella ⇢ Real Madrid, £50mTyrique George ⇢ Everton, £24mAlejandro Garnacho ⇢ Aston Villa, Loan.

Ramos, Diawara, Nkunku, Fofana, Tomori, Athekame, Odogu, Jashari, Bartesaghi, Vladimirov, Pittarella, Gabbia, Saelemakers, Cisse, Musah.

The English forward joined Chelsea from Borussia Dortmund last summer for just under £50m. He struggled to make an impact last season in his first year at Chelsea, failing to register a goal in the Premier League or Champions League but did spend most of the second half of last season on the sidelines due to an injury. Gittens, who is on the bench for Chelsea today, has been speaking this week to CFC+:.

Recent findings suggest that “I am feeling, I would say, more confident now, in my body as well. The injury that happened [impacted my first season], but I am feeling better every day. I am trying to improve every day to be the best version of myself. It has been good to be back with the boys. I am really enjoying it right now and it has been really good to be part of this team.”.

According to recent reports, have a great day, Jamie. 🥳 pic.twitter.com/QeX83XrXAM.

According to recent reports, in Chelsea’s defeat to Juventus in midweek, Ukrainian forward Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 after a long doping ban was resolved. You can read all about that game right here. Mudryk is on the bench for Chelsea today.

Our line-up to face AC Milan! pic.twitter.com/MK2hd0c708.

Current Chelsea defender Tosin Adarabioyo has been catching up with former Chelsea men Ruben Loftus-Cheek, who starts for AC Milan today, and Fikayo Tomori.

The team news is in from Jakarta! 🗞️ pic.twitter.com/BRBjmlgwz8.

In a recent development, the atmosphere is building. 🇮🇩📈 pic.twitter.com/fhXfDVAf6s.

Chelsea’s pre-season continues out in the Far East as they take on AC Milan in the Gelora Bung Karno Stadium in Jakarta, Indonesia. Both clubs now have latest managers, with Xabi Alonso taking over at Chelsea and former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim now at the helm at AC Milan. These sides met in pre-season last year, with Chelsea winning 4-1 at Stamford Bridge. At that time, now-Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca was in charge whilst Max Allegri, who is now at Napoli, was leading AC Milan. The last time they met competitively was during the 2022/23 Champions League season, with Chelsea winning both games.

Chelsea lost 1-0 to AC Milan’s Serie A rivals Juventus on Wednesday in Hong Kong, in which Danny Welbeck made his first Chelsea appearance after joining from Brighton in the last week.

According to recent reports, “We want to have a great team spirit and that is built on a daily basis with a great culture in the building,” Alonso mentioned in his pre-match press conference. “That helps in the moment you have to compete. You feel better having that togetherness, trust, and the bonds between the players are so vital to ultimately building a winning mentality, and a team that can compete anywhere. So the football side is so important, but the mental side is as important. And the strength of the team is the most important. We have been able to train and prepare [during pre-season] and I am very happy with the attitude and personality, we know that it is a very important part of this tour.”.

According to recent reports, it has been another busy week on the transfer front for Chelsea; not only has Welbeck arrived over the last week but so too have Jordan Henderson and Valentin Barco. Alonso’s men have two more games after this against Johor Darul Ta’zim and Real Sociedad before getting their Premier League campaign under way with a derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage.

It has been revealed that AC Milan finished fifth in Serie A last season to earn a spot in the Europa League last season. Their big-money acquisition this summer as been Portuguese striker Goncalo Ramos from PSG. They have played two pre-season friendlies so far, which have both ended in draws; 2-2 against Celtic and then 1-1 against city rivals Inter. They kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

Starting with Mike Maignan, both he and the French medical staff have reassured Milan regarding the physical matter that forced the goalkeeper to be substituted at half-time during Sunday’s match between Les Bleus and Turkey.

Bournemouth injury news: Marco Rose reveals Alex Scott start strategy ahead of Nottingham Forest clash

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (341 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Ben Sully | 19 Nov 2026 21:26.
  • Bournemouth boss Marco Rose has revealed Alex Scott will start at least one of the next three competitive matches.
  • Scott has not played for Bournemouth since September after sustaining a thigh injury in England’s 7-0 win over Croatia at the start of October.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Sully | 19 Nov 2026 21:26.

Bournemouth boss Marco Rose has revealed Alex Scott will start at least one of the next three competitive matches.

Scott has not played for Bournemouth since September after sustaining a thigh injury in England’s 7-0 win over Croatia at the start of October.

The midfielder missed the next eight matches before he returned to the matchday squad for the 2-1 victory over Ipswich Town before the international window.

However, Rose opted against risking Scott at Portman Road, giving him the chance to build up his fitness over the two-week break.

Bournemouth will resume their campaign with a home meeting with Nottingham Forest on Saturday, before they head on their travels for games against Celta Vigo and Fulham in the Europa League and Premier League respectively.

Speaking ahead of Saturday’s fixture, Rose has confirmed that Scott will start at least one of the next three matches for the Cherries.

"We have many games in the upcoming weeks. Next week we have three games, so there are a lot of choices.” Rose said in Thursday’s pre-match press conference.

“For sure, he is going to start one game in this. We have to increase the match time step by step.".

Forward Junior Kroupi missed the first two months of the season after undergoing foot surgery in the summer.

As a result, Rose was keen to exercise caution when Kroupi returned to action last month, handing him four substitute appearances before he linked up with Zinedine Zidane's France squad.

Kroupi made his international debut in the 3-1 defeat to Italy before he scored his first goal for France in Sunday's 2-1 win over Turkey.

While both of those appearances came from the bench, Rose has now provided an enhancement on whether Kroupi is in a position to start games.

"Junior is ready to get more match time and even to start," the Bournemouth boss remarked.

In regard to absentees, the Cherries are likely to be without Juanlu Sanchez, Julian Araujo and Alex Toth.

#38432. England's Euro 2028 mission starts NOW! Thomas Tuchel's men must beat Spain to prove they can compete with the best - or risk their 'DNA' cursing them yet again, writes OLIVER HOLT

📅 14 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1327 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

England's Euro 2028 mission starts NOW! Thomas Tuchel's men must beat Spain to prove they can compete with the best - or risk their 'DNA' cursing them yet again, writes OLIVER HOLT

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1327 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 16:10 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 19:04 EST, 14 November 2026.
  • It is four months, almost to the day, since England shrank from the call of history and lost their World Cup semi-final to Argentina in Atlanta but Thomas Tuchel may not believe that the Nations League tie against Spain in the Metropolitano on Sunday evening represents his best shot at redemption for the way things played out that afternoon in America’s South.
  • It has been revealed that that is largely because Tuchel does not appear to believe he has anything to redeem himself for.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By OLIVER HOLT, CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 16:10 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 19:04 EST, 14 November 2026.

It is four months, almost to the day, since England shrank from the call of history and lost their World Cup semi-final to Argentina in Atlanta but Thomas Tuchel may not believe that the Nations League tie against Spain in the Metropolitano on Sunday evening represents his best shot at redemption for the way things played out that afternoon in America’s South.

It has been revealed that that is largely because Tuchel does not appear to believe he has anything to redeem himself for. The manner of his side’s capitulation - and the substitutions he made - in the Mercedes-Benz Stadium last July enraged the nation, but Tuchel stated the fault was in the damned DNA of the English, that we were underlings, and that our players found it constitutionally impossible to keep hold of the ball.

Whatever Tuchel thinks, the fact remains that the tie against Lamine Yamal, Fabian Ruiz, Pedri and Mikel Oyarzabal and the rest of the world champions at the home of Atletico Madrid offers Tuchel and his players the opportunity to encourage themselves and their fans that they are not destined to be also-rans wired to fall at the final hurdle for evermore.

Spain are formidable opposition. They are on a record-breaking run of 43 matches unbeaten and have won their last 12 in succession. They haven't drawn a game since their June 15 game against Cape Verde in the World Cup. Their last defeat was on March 22, 2024, when they lost 1-0 to Colombia in a friendly. Some ask whether they are the best international side the world has ever seen.

‘Spain seem unbeatable,’ Tuchel noted, when he walked into the press room at the Metropolitano on Saturday night and heard hymns of praise being lavished upon the opponents he is about to face.

According to recent reports, ‘They have a very strong identity and a very strong mentality. We are trying to take it away from them. We are up for it. We are up for the fight. We are up for a spectacular match. We can see how far we can push the limits with the world champions in Madrid. The group is full of self-belief and rightly so.’.

England must beat Spain to prove they can compete with the best - even if they have flaws.

Thomas Tuchel must show he can find a way around the limitations presented by the 'DNA' he has complained about.

Industry observers note that this may be the toughest game that Tuchel’s England side play until the European Championships in 2028, where the final will be contested at Wembley, and they will play all their games at home. They need to go into that tournament with the belief that they can beat the best when the pressure is at its highest.

In a recent development, beating Spain away in the final game of the group phase of the Nations League is not quite the same as a critical match at a major tournament but it is as stiff a challenge as Tuchel is going to face until then. Beating Croatia 7-0 in front of gangs of schoolkids in Rijeka last month was hailed as the best England performance of the Tuchel era. Which claims it all, really.

In a recent development, it was a great performance in a relatively meaningless match. Now it is time for him to show that he can marshal an England side to succeed against the very best, not fall apart when the prize is in sight. His protestations of powerlessness in the aftermath of the Argentina defeat were not a good look for a coach who was hired with the idea that his coaching prowess and his game management could get England over the line.

Has he learned anything from the manner of the Argentina defeat? ‘This game against Spain will be proof of concept at the highest level,’ he said, ‘but we are up for it. I think we have taken the next step after the World Cup. The best thing is to trust our process and trust ourselves. We need to be clear about how we want to impose ourselves and I think that is all visible.’.

Now it is time for him to show that he can find a way past the limitations of England’s footballing DNA, find a way to compete with Spain and France when it really matters, and find a way to end the culture of near misses that has come to be England’s lot in the last decade of appearances in semi-finals and finals.

Sources indicate that england have played six matches since that day of crushing disappointment in Atlanta and scored 22 goals. But in the only one of those matches that really mattered, they lost 3-2 to Spain at Wembley in the opening tie of their Nations League campaign at the end of September, a game in which they were largely outclassed by Luis de la Fuente’s team.

In a recent development, spain are what England have to aim for. Tuchel mentioned their example and their ability and their mindset straight after the semi-final loss to Argentina. ‘Ball possession plays a crucial role,’ he noted at his post-match press conference in Atlanta. ‘It’s maybe not in our DNA like it is in our Spanish DNA or in our Argentinian-Brazilian DNA, to take the ball and control the game with the ball.’.

This may well be their toughest game until the final of the 2028 European Championships, if they get that far.

The England coach remarked more recently that England need to go back to trusting a traditional style that emphasises direct, high-intensity physicality rather than trying to copy Spanish patience in ball-retention. England, though, were taught a lesson in sophistication by the Spanish in September.

According to recent reports, and for all the attention lavished on Yamal, Spain’s defence is the best in the world. Rodri, the shield for that defence and also the world’s best in the role, is not fit for this game but even without him, Spain’s back-line inspires an awful lot more confidence than England’s.

‘They were the best in the World Cup at the back,’ Declan Rice, England’s central midfielder, remarked on Saturday. ‘Defence wins you titles. Everyone talks about their attacking talent but you look at their central defenders, their full backs and the way their midfielders contribute to the defence, too.’.

That defence will have to stop England’s resurgent front line, led by Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane, who could be flanked by Anthony Gordon and Morgan Rogers and backed up by the supreme talent of Jude Bellingham just behind them.

Recent findings suggest that bellingham’s improving relationship with Tuchel, which cannot have been harmed by the inclusion of Bellingham’s brother, Jobe, in this squad, is another reason to hope that England still retain the capacity to improve after the World Cup. The elder Bellingham has become England’s most influential player.

England at their best would be one of the few teams capable of extending them. Rice said on Saturday that the game between the two sides was ‘massive’. England need to prove they can find a way to get closer to the world champions. To beat them, Rice said, would be a ‘massive statement’.

‘Playing against them is a great incentive to win. It will show where we are as a group. We are trying to attack teams full throttle and with players like Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham and Morgan Rogers in our attack, it feels as if it is going to take off one night and maybe tomorrow night will be the night. We can beat Spain. For sure, we can.’.

Tuchel needs to prove England can win, not just be noble contenders. They need to prove that their DNA need not be a curse.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, sheffield United let the attacker head out the exit door on a temporary basis again in the summer to help him get some more experience under his belt. He has since flourished away from SUFC and they will be pleased with his development in League Two.

Marsh, 22, has enjoyed plenty of game time with the Spirerites under the guidance of their head coach Paul Cook and he has become one of their key players over recent times. He has made 16 appearances in all competitions in this campaign, 12 of which have come in the league, and he has chipped in with an eye-catching eight goals and three assists to date.

It has been revealed that he is due to return to the Blades next year and he remains under contract with the South Yorkshire outfit until June 2028 so still just under two years left to run down. Chris Wilder should have him in his long-term prepares after his impressive campaign to date.

Sheffield United are aiming to get into the Championship play-offs this term. They are sat in 10th place and are two points off the top eight behind both QPR and Southampton after 15 fixtures.

Sheffield United will see Marsh as one for the future. He is versatile and can play as a centre-forward or as an attacking midfielder which means he will be a useful weapon for SUFC down the line.

At the age of 22, he has bags of potential and the capacity to improve over the coming years. The Blades will be keeping tabs on his development at Chesterfield and will be satisfied with how he is doing.

The ex-England youth international, who played for the Three Lions’ U20s side back in 2024, has risen up through the academy at Bramall Lane. He was a regular at various different youth levels.

Recent findings suggest that marsh has played five times for Sheffield United’s senior team to date. Prior to his switch to Chesterfield, he was loaned out to Doncaster Rovers, Fleetwood Town and Falkirk to get some exposure to men’s football.

In a recent development, sheffield United have an option to extend Patrick Bamford‘s stay until 2028. However, there are question marks over the long-term futures of Tyrese Campbell, Tom Cannon and Jordan Ayes, whilst Romelle Donovan and Ben Brereton Diaz will return to Brentford and Southampton respectively next year.

Recent findings suggest that therefore, the Blades will be short of attacking options by next term. That means that Marsh has an ideal opportunity to stake a claim when he is back from Chesterfield.

After failing to complete their defence in the final days of the summer transfer window, AC Milan will try again in January.

In a recent development, the defensive depth is rather limited amid Matteo Gabbia’s lengthy injury absence, while Fikayo Tomori also sustained an issue, meaning a reinforcement in that area of ​​the pitch will be needed in January. Ruben Amorim’s number one target has not changed from the summer.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

This morning’s edition of Corriere dello Sport (via MilanNews) confirms the No.1 centre-back target: Goncalo Inacio. Milan tried to snatch him from Sporting CP in August, but the Portuguese club repeatedly turned them down, having already sold Ousmane Diomande to Nottingham Forest.

Sources indicate that the Rossoneri haven’t abandoned the idea of ​​reuniting him with Amorim, and so in January they will make another attempt for the 25-year-old, who is eager to join a top club. However, a significant offer of at least €40m will be needed to convince Sporting.

The management believe that another central defender is needed too, so they’re starting to monitor some prospects for next summer. Among the players being closely monitored is Gabriele Calvani, who is on loan at Frosinone from Genoa.

He has impressed so far and has a current valuation of €10m that could rise. For now, signing a young prospect isn’t a priority for the Rossoneri, as they are primarily looking for someone who can slot immediately into the starting XI.

Mauricio Pochettino's record vs Liverpool: Can he overcome Reds litmus test on Man Utd managerial debut?

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (824 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Saikat Mandal | 19 Nov 2026 21:29, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 20:08.
  • Mauricio Pochettino has taken the plunge into unfinished Premier League business, accepting the daunting challenge of taking charge of Manchester United at arguably the lowest ebb in their modern history.
  • Since Sir Alex Ferguson's departure, the Red Devils have endured a steady and, at times, bewildering decline, although few could have envisaged the club spiralling to such depths.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Saikat Mandal | 19 Nov 2026 21:29, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 20:08.

Mauricio Pochettino has taken the plunge into unfinished Premier League business, accepting the daunting challenge of taking charge of Manchester United at arguably the lowest ebb in their modern history.

Since Sir Alex Ferguson's departure, the Red Devils have endured a steady and, at times, bewildering decline, although few could have envisaged the club spiralling to such depths.

Sitting in the bottom three of the Premier League table after 10 games, Man Utd find themselves navigating one of the darkest chapters of their history in more than two decades.

Michael Carrick had offered plenty of promise last season after steering the club back into the Champions League, but that resurgence proved painfully short-lived, with the momentum failing to carry into the new campaign and the hierarchy eventually losing patience with the Englishman.

A total of 11 managers, including interim appointments, have come and gone since 2013, and while the Old Trafford hotseat retains its considerable allure, the red carpet awaiting its latest occupant has long since been replaced by a bed of nails.

By accepting the offer, Pochettino has willingly grasped the poisoned chalice, although he could yet emerge as the Red Devils' long-awaited Messiah if he is afforded the time and authority to mould the squad in his own image and build something capable of enduring.

A trip to Anfield represents the ultimate litmus test for any Manchester United manager, and Pochettino could hardly have been handed a more imposing introduction to life in the Old Trafford dugout.

The two most successful clubs in English football share a rivalry of extraordinary magnitude, one whose history, intensity and cultural significance are difficult to replicate anywhere else in Europe's major leagues.

Curiously, however, it has been a rarity for both sides to enjoy their periods of absolute dominance simultaneously, with the balance of power traditionally swinging one way before shifting back after a prolonged spell.

Liverpool ruled the roost throughout much of the 1970s and 1980s, before the Red Devils seized the mantle and established themselves as England's pre-eminent force over the following two decades.

That hierarchy has shifted once again, with Liverpool restoring their position among the country's leading powers and adding two more league titles to their illustrious collection.

Pochettino's immediate priority will be to drag Man Utd out of their current mire, but the longer-term ambition must surely extend beyond mere recovery: restoring the club's former stature and, ultimately, knocking Liverpool off their perch once again.

Across his managerial career, the 54-year-old has faced Liverpool 19 times, winning three, drawing five and suffering 11 defeats, a record that makes for sobering reading ahead of his latest meeting with the Reds.

One of those losses came on the grandest stage of all: the Champions League final, when Divock Origi struck the decisive goal to etch his name into Anfield folklore and condemn Pochettino's Tottenham Hotspur to defeat.

Curiously, however, some of the Argentine's most memorable moments against Liverpool came when he was managing Southampton.

Back in 2013, Pochettino, then still a relatively unheralded figure in English football, masterminded a tactical masterclass at Anfield, where Southampton suffocated Liverpool's attacking threat with an aggressive press executed with remarkable discipline and control.

The Saints emerged with a famous 1-0 victory, providing an early glimpse of Pochettino's tactical credentials before his subsequent move to north London.

His time at Tottenham, by contrast, proved considerably less fruitful against the Merseyside giants, with Pochettino managing just one victory in 13 meetings.

That solitary success came in emphatic fashion, as Spurs swept Liverpool aside 4-1 at Wembley Stadium during their temporary stay at the ground in the 2017-18 campaign, while he also oversaw a 1-1 draw against the Reds during his brief spell at Chelsea.

Few would blame Pochettino if Man Utd were to come away from Anfield empty-handed, particularly given the lack of time he has had to prepare his side for such a daunting assignment, while even a hard-fought draw would represent an excellent result.

Having arrived at Old Trafford at such a turbulent juncture, it would be unrealistic to expect the Argentine to weave his magic overnight, but the Red Devils arguably need him now more than he needs them, with the club crying out for direction, stability and a clearly defined footballing identity.

Through meticulous coaching, astute recruitment and, crucially, the unwavering backing of the hierarchy, Pochettino could gradually restore the foundations that have been missing for so long and give the Red Devils a genuine platform from which to rise again.

For now, though, the Argentine must resist the temptation to look too far ahead and simply embrace the challenge in front of him, because while the Anfield cauldron represents a formidable first examination, it also offers him an opportunity to make an early statement and begin a upcoming chapter at Manchester United on his own terms.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 19 Nov 2026 21:32.

Tottenham Hotspur are sweating over the availability of James Maddison ahead of Saturday's Premier League encounter with Ipswich Town, with question marks remaining over whether the attacking midfielder will be fit enough to feature.

Roberto De Zerbi is contending with a lengthy list of injury doubts, as Mykhaylo Mudryk, Martin Dubravka, Savio, Mathys Tel, Lucas Bergvall and Tosin Adarabioyo all face late assessments for various ankle, knee, muscle and calf concerns, while Xavi Simons and Wilson Odobert remain sidelined with knee problems.

With Dubravka doubtful, Antonin Kinsky is poised to retain the gloves between the sticks behind a four-man rearguard featuring Pedro Porro, Micky van de Ven, Andy Robertson and Jan Paul van Hecke.

Remarkably, no Spurs player has scored more league goals than Van Hecke this term, a notable statistic for the two-goal centre-back as the hosts prepare to welcome the Tractor Boys.

In the engine room, Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes are expected to form a central midfield partnership to dictate the tempo of the contest.

Further forward, Archie Gray could be deployed in an advanced central role if Maddison is not risked from the off, flanked by Mohammed Kudus and Omar Marmoush in a dynamic creative trio.

Although Kudus has yet to score a league goal this season, the playmaker's three assists and ability to threaten from unlikely positions make him a potential match-winner for the home side.

Leading the line will be Dominic Solanke, who will look to capitalise on that creative service and spearhead the North Londoners to maximum points on Saturday afternoon.

Tottenham Hotspur possible starting lineup:.

Kinsky; Porro, Van Hecke, Van de Ven, Robertson; Tonali, Fernandes; Kudus, Gray, Marmoush; Solanke.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Michael Carrick stated he had to be careful with Mason Mount after the England midfielder handed Manchester United an injury scare in their friendly draw with Paris St Germain.

Mount has had a torrid time with injuries since signing from Chelsea in a £55m-deal three years ago, starting only 25 Premier League games for United in that time.

The 27-year-old has been successfully deployed by Carrick in a central midfield role during pre-season, leading to speculation that United may not make another expected signing in that department.

But Mount played only 18 minutes of Saturday’s 1-1 draw against the European champions in Gothenburg before being replaced by Scotland international Tyler Fletcher.

It has been revealed that “He [Mount] got kicked. We just wanted to be careful and look after him,” Carrick, the United head coach, told reporters in Sweden.

“We’ve been lucky with injuries so far, so we wanted to be careful.”.

Post-match video footage showed Mount walking freely on to the United bus without the aid of a protective boot or knee support.

According to recent reports, michael Carrick told VG Mason Mount was taken off as a precaution. Looked OK leaving stadium. pic.twitter.com/Uo0fBtgpAl.

United went behind within two minutes at the Ullevi Stadium when Liverpool target Ibrahim Mbaye punished slack marking to put PSG ahead.

Bryan Mbeumo fired United level after 32 minutes following good work from Amad Diallo, the Cameroon forward’s third goal in two games after his match-winning double against Atletico Madrid.

United meet Leeds in a Dublin friendly on Wednesday before coming up against AC Milan and their former manager Ruben Amorim next Saturday.

United open their Premier League campaign at Hull on August 22.

Industry observers note that “It was good game. PSG is good so we had to keep building fitness. I am happy to have other [players] back and we have to keep going.”.

“It’s good for me. I enjoyed it. We need to build fitness, we have a massive season ahead.”.

“It’s a good game PSG are tough to beat and we got a draw and now think about the next game [against Leeds in Dublin].”.

It has been revealed that “We have two more games against Leeds a and Milan. We need to have big season and hope to win a trophy.”.

Industry observers note that all over in Gothenburg and it’s been a good match for Michael Carrick’s team. They looked sharper and quicker than their win over Atletico Madrid last week (what the manager wanted) and things are moving in the right direction. Two things to worry about, however, were the early exits of Mason Mount and Tom Heaton with injuries. They’ll especially hope the Mount knock isn’t anything mid or long term.

Nearly done and it’s been a good run out for United. They’ve looked the better, sharper side and, if anything, deserve to win. In mitigation, this is United fourth pre-season game to PSG’s second...

Fernandes has one thing on his mind when he gets the ball 25 yards out in the centre of the park - a shot. He unleashes the attempt, destined for the bottom-left corner, forcing Longoni, the sub goalkeeper, into a good save.

Sources indicate that two chances for United in quick succession. A lovely ball from the middle of the park by Zirkzee finds Dalot on the right. He chips the ball to the back post where one of the Fletchers (sorry, I am not sure which) heads for goal. His attempt is blocked and the ball, ultimately, falls at the feet of Lacey whose shot is blazed high over the bar.

There have been plenty of good things for Carrick to take from this match. The passing, while not of the standard of a cut-and-thrust Premier League match, has been good for the time of year, and there have been enough flashes of brilliance/class/invention etc to suggest that pre-season is moving in the right direction.

Industry observers note that lovely bit of play by United. A great pass with the outside of the boot from the inside-left channel by Tielemans finds Fernandes who plays a sidefooted shot that goes just wide.

Tielemans’s first bit of brilliance from the Belgian there.

Sources indicate that both sides losing possession a fair bit at the moment. Strong pre-season vibes right now.

Sources indicate that maguire has had a good game. He’s played a number of long passes from the back and looked assured. This time he’s up in the PSG half and decides to have a pop - his shot testing Safanov, who saves well.

Had there been VAR Safanov might have had something to answer for...he may have beaten Zirkzee to the ball but he flew in the air and jurt the United man in the process.

Anwway, there’s no VAR (hurrah, for those of you who consider it a modern-day evil) and it doesn’t matter.

Chance for United to go ahead and it comes from two things. (i) A long, hopeful ball from Fernandes that looks for Zirkzee (ii) Safanov rushing off his line and into no-man’s land. The ball comes loose and Jack Fletcher, instead of having a go at goal, with the keeper on the ground and out of the game, passes to Lacey whose shot is wide.

Tyler Fletcher loses the ball near the United half and it, ultimately, results in a PSG corner. From the set piece United defend well and snuff out all hint of danger.

PSG seeing more of the ball at the moment. They work the ball to the right and Amass brings down Mbaye.

From the resulting free-kick, in the final third, the French side whip in the ball but Mee is up ot the challenge and come to collect well.

Santos, Mbeumo, Shaw, Amad, Lacey are off.

Fernandes, Jack Feltcher, Zirkzee and Amass are on.

And it’s a debut for Tielemans.

A raft of changes for PSG sees Marquinhos and João Neves, among others, come on. More like it, in terms of first-team ‘names’, on the pitch for the European Cup champions.

United on top in this half, as they were in the first.

According to recent reports, the paces quickens and the game is much better for it. Mbuemo drives toward the PSG box, he cuts inside from the right before unleashing a shot that is bound for the back of the net before a fine one-handed save by Safanov. Credit, too, for Maguire whose long ball from the back found Mbuemo brilliantly. Promising...

Lacey tries to play in Dorgu on the left but he’s asking too much of his team-mate. Wonder when the expected raft of changes will take place?

Slow start to the second half. This is very much pre-season-friendly pace.

In a recent development, having seen Mount limp off in the first half, there’s more worry at the start of the second and Heaton is force off with what looks like a hamstrung injury. He dashed off his line to clear a ball and in doing so has tweaked something. Mee replaces him.

Back under way Gothenburg - there have been a number of changes and will bring them to you once I’ve worked out who has come on and who they’ve replaced.

A world record that still stands...(this was back in 1995).

In a recent development, and that is it for the first 45 minutes. PSG took the early lead, but from that moment on United have been the better side and deservedly are level through Mbueno’s goal.

There will be one minute of added time at the end of what has been a good first half for Man Utd.

Industry observers note that amad has a go from outside the box forcing the save from Safanov. He’s such a live wire and one of the best in his position in the top flight. Him or Antony? No contest, strange it took United a while to work that one out.

In a recent development, yet more good work from the underrated Amad. He again closes down well on the right before winning back possession and cutting the ball back for Lacey. To think he was starring for Sunderland in the Championship while Antony was starting for United...

United have been the better side since conceding earlier and, as if to illustrate my point, as I typed that an Mbuemo free-kick is well saved by Safanov. That was heading for the top-right bin.

Great work on the left by Dorgu and Shaw ends with the latter chipping the ball to the back post where Amad is lurking with intent. The Ivorian looks to head the ball home, but before he can get anything on it it looks as though he’s pushed in the back. United players are sure it’s a penalty but, more importantly, the referee doesn’t.

Amad does brilliantly, winning the ball off Koukaba in the final third, from there he scampers toward the box before playing in Mbuemo who takes one touch before firing in a shot into the bottom right corner of the net.

Free-kick for PSG on the right, near the final third. The ball comes in and it’s straight into the arms of Heaton in the United goal.

Kvaratskhelia, not seen much of him so far, runs into the box, but Amad does well to usher him back out.

The match is pedestrian at the moment, but as I type that, Dorgu, yep, him again, drives down the left and puts in a good cross that is well intercepted by Safanov in the PSG goal.

United continue to see more of the ball, Dorgu’s seeing more of it than most. But, no chances really fashioned, still, plenty of time to go.

Worry for United having to sub off Mount. It looks as though he took a knock to a foot and Carrick and co will hope it’s not a long-term injury. Mount, who’s had a good pre-season, has been replaced by Fletcher, son of Darren.

Industry observers note that foul on Mazraoui results in two things. The Mount has to come off, and, United have a free-kick on the edge of the PSG area.

From the set-piece Mbuemo has a go and it’s a regulation save from Safonov in the PSG goal.

It has been revealed that heaven loses possession in the middle of the park and from there it’s like the parting of the Red Sea as PSG have a three-on-one. Mbaye gets the shot in on goal but Andrey Santos covers back brilliantly and does enough to get something on the ball. He’s started both this match and pre-season well.

Sources indicate that united are looking half decent on the ball. They’re passing it well and not afraid to switch things around.

It has been revealed that A lovely long ball from Maguire finds Dorgo whose lovely first touch takes him into the box before a cut back is intercepted by a PSG man. Promising signs though for Carrick’s men.

United seeing more of the ball at the moment. They’re being patient but cannot fashion an opening and the ball is worked all the way back to Heaton in goal.

Needless to say this is being played at a slowish pace...no blood-and-guts challenges being put in.

Industry observers note that good work down the right sees Amad plays in Shay Lacey who crosses into the box. The ball find shte head of Mbuemo and the ball sails over the bar. Better from United.

United started slowly against Atletico and they’ve done the same here.

Bright start to say the least from the French side. They work the ball left and it’s an easy cross from Dro Fernandez for Mbaye to tap home for the very early lead.

Recent findings suggest that they’re under way in Sweden. United are in their latest vibrant red kit and PSG in their blue, red and white kit. Significant fan of the French side’s kit, it harks back to the kit they had in the 1990s when the likes of George Weah and David Ginola were entertaining in the capital of France.

A reminder of how they line up.

According to recent reports, man Utd: Heaton, Mazraoui, Maguire, Heaven, Shaw, Mount, Santos, Dorgu, Lacey, Amad, Mbeumo; Subs: Heath, Mee, Amass, Armer, Dalot, Yoro, Fernandes, J. Fletcher, T. Fletcher, Tielemans, Zirkzee.

Paris St-Germain: Safonov, Pacho, Zabarnyi, Koukaba, Boly, Beraldo, Dro, Mayulu, Kvaratskhelia, Ayari, Mbaye; Subs: Marquinhos, Mendes, Lucea, Vitinha, Neves, El Nay, Idder, Drame, Bourdin, Ndjantou, Meite, Longoni, Chevalier.

And here’s a famous match that took place there, giving a certain Sir Alex Ferguson his first European trophy.

“Get a bit sharper, get better on the ball, go up a notch.”.

“It’s not about today it’s about preparing. Some players have played 90 minutes, some have played three games, some have just come back. So it’s about keeping working on things we’ve been working on.”.

In a recent development, “They’re similar to us, but have fewer senior players available . They’ve had a great time and great squad so whoever on the pitch it will be a test.”.

A hugely talented player for a number of clubs, including United, who ever really lived up to his early promise.

Here’s a goal to dine out on...

Good to have you back, lads 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/3EgkXLqcQm.

📃 Le onze de départ pour cette rencontre de préparation face à Manchester United. #PSGMUN pic.twitter.com/LodcDM1Yrm.

I expect they’ll make an appearence at some point.

Ready to face PSG in our latest pre-season test ✊.

Manchester United continue their Sweden sojourn with match against Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg.

Clearly a clash against the back-to-back Champions League winners is a step up from their previous two pre-season friendlies (victories against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid), but at the same time this is more a chance for players to get miles in the legs and see how new signings and possibly some young guns fit in.

Recent findings suggest that one of those new signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

Michael Carrick has also been boosted by the returns of Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui after their post-World Cup breaks.

Industry observers note that cunha, however, will not play a part in today’s match because of a “minor illness” according to the MUTV website. He is expected to link up with the squad in Ireland, where they face Leeds United at Croke Park, after the match.

This will be Man Utd’s first outing since the 2-1 win over Atletico, a performance and result that pleased Carrick.

“I enjoyed it, I thought there was a lot of good in things that we are looking to improve on,” the United manager mentioned. “Building on what we did for the last seven months, I think there is a lot of good signs for us, it’s never going to be the exact stage we want to be at. But I thought there was really a lot of positives to take out of the game, individual, collectively as a team, senior players looking strong and fit, and the younger players doing really well.

“The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s manufacturer. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”.

Kick-off is set for 4pm so stay here for the build up, team news and action.

Man United head coach Mauricio Pochettino is "the right character" for the Red Devils but he has "a lot to prove"

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1023 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Matt Law | 19 Nov 2026 22:09, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 09:06.
  • Ahead of Manchester United's trip to Liverpool in the Premier League on Sunday, Sports Mole's Football Editor Matt Law discusses what will be Mauricio Pochettino's first match in charge of the 20-time English champions.
  • United have only won one Premier League game this season, so there are no easy games at the moment.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 19 Nov 2026 22:09, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 09:06.

Ahead of Manchester United's trip to Liverpool in the Premier League on Sunday, Sports Mole's Football Editor Matt Law discusses what will be Mauricio Pochettino's first match in charge of the 20-time English champions.

A nice easy start. United have only won one Premier League game this season, so there are no easy games at the moment.

It is a quick turnaround for Pochettino. He had the second USA game against Haiti, finishing at midnight UK time on Tuesday, then flew straight to England and into Carrington to begin work, and was back in again today, Thursday, to prepare.

The preparations are far from ideal with players coming back from international duty, but they are what they are. I think what will be very interesting going forward is the shape Pochettino settles on. I still think it will be a 4-2-3-1 for the majority.

Sources indicate that we know Pochettino likes high pressing and fast attacking transitions. There are suggestions he likes Marcus Rashford a lot, though perhaps more the Rashford of a few years ago than the one who has been injured and is potentially coming back in.

Industry observers note that he likes his full-backs to attack. The counter-pressing. He likes his attacking midfielders to be creative, so expect Bruno Fernandes to be given fewer defensive duties and more of a free role in that number 10 position.

Pochettino spoke about mentality and togetherness, the culture, and he will want his team aligned. There are no suggestions the players threw Carrick under the bus.

Ultimately it was a mixture of Carrick not being tactically good enough and the players not responding in the end to the management style. The change had to happen.

According to recent reports, he speaks on Friday afternoon and will give a team news update at that point. Suggestions are that Harry Maguire had a slight injury in the Villa game but should be fine. Luke Shaw may or may not be fit. Marcus Rashford may or may not be fit. There will be no Sesko. There will be no Baleba. Lisandro Martinez is back from his suspension.

Patrick Dorgu is back too. He did not play for Denmark over the break but came off the bench to great effect against Villa last time out.

Suddenly there are a lot more options in the defensive areas of the pitch, which has been the major problem for Man United this season.

The midfield is going to be interesting for this game. Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo started against Villa. Andrey Santos is an option in that area of the field as well.

It has been revealed that mason Mount has played there, but I am not convinced by Mount in central midfield. Baleba being out is a substantial one, because I feel he could be a key player under Pochettino.

There are suggestions he will be out for a shorter period than initially thought after picking up that muscular injury against Roma in the Champions League.

In a recent development, can Dorgu get himself back in the team? He could be a massive player for them going forward. But for now, the key thing is getting the team together and working out how they are going to play.

Recent findings suggest that there is no rest for the wicked either. They go to Portugal next week for the Sporting Lisbon game in the Champions League, then welcome Brentford, then Newcastle and Coventry, then back in Champions League action against Leipzig.

This period is incredibly busy. The fact that Pochettino was appointed at the end of last week and then had to wait through that second USA game is not ideal, but we have had ideal preparations before and it has still gone wrong anyway.

Industry observers note that I do like the Pochettino appointment. He has got a lot to prove. He seems like the right character, and you can tell he really wanted this job.

Recent findings suggest that it is the job he has been linked with numerous times without it ever coming off. Now feels like the right time, and hopefully United can get something against Liverpool.

It has been revealed that united's recent record against Liverpool is good. Three games unbeaten, winning both Premier League games last season, including that 2-1 win at Anfield with that late Harry Maguire header.

Sources indicate that united are down in 18th in the Premier League: one win, five draws, four defeats. Fourteen goals scored is not awful. Nineteen goals conceded is awful.

Gary Neville mentioned recently that the back four that finished against Villa would get you relegated, and it is difficult to argue against that, but it should be strengthened for this match.

One Premier League win all season is diabolical. Ultimately it is why Carrick lost his job. But the recent performance against Villa, getting two late goals and avoiding defeat, was a major positive.

Going forward, the story is Pochettino, but it is also the players. Where is the professional pride? Can there be a bit more solidity at the back and an end to the defensive errors?

Senne Lammens has had a good start to his career but questions are now being asked. There are a few shots going in around him that he really should be doing better with, and what is happening in front of him is not helping in that regard.

I would like to see a settled team in the Premier League. Changes have to happen for European games, but get a settled team, get the system playing, get Fernandes in his best position, and get the wingers sorted, whether that is Rashford. Amad Diallo has not scored in almost a year now, so he may have to come out of the team.

Sources indicate that I think you are keeping Mbeumo through the middle. Cunha has been decent of late. He has got the players there. Looking forward to this one and we will see what Pochettino can come up with.

West Brom have to consider deal to re-sign Ipswich Town man in January transfer window: Opinion

💡 Key Takeaways
  • West Brom will get the chance to bring in some upcoming faces this winter ahead of the second-half of the season.
  • The Baggies were dealt a blow at the start of last month when Noah Galves was ruled out for the rest of the campaign with a serious knee injury.
  • Industry observers note that step forward Ipswich Town defender Darnell Furlong, who could be made available due to a lack of game time at Portman Road following the Tractor Boys’ promotion to the Premier League.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Brom will get the chance to bring in some upcoming faces this winter ahead of the second-half of the season. WBA are right now in the Championship play-offs along with Stoke City, Wolves, Swansea City, Southampton and QPR after 15 fixtures.

The Baggies were dealt a blow at the start of last month when Noah Galves was ruled out for the rest of the campaign with a serious knee injury. That has left them short of options at full-back and they would benefit from another option to battle with Brayann Pereira.

Industry observers note that step forward Ipswich Town defender Darnell Furlong, who could be made available due to a lack of game time at Portman Road following the Tractor Boys’ promotion to the Premier League. He was on the books at The Hawthorns from 2019 to 2025 and made 247 appearances in all competitions for the Midlands outfit, chipping in with 11 goals from the back.

It has been revealed that west Brom could get the opportunity now to try and lure him back in some capacity. They are back in action this weekend with an away trip to Swansea City.

Furlong is under contract at Ipswich Town until June 2028. However, he has slipped down the pecking order in Suffolk and has made only three outings so far this term, one one of which has come in the league.

A change of scene to West Brom would make sense for him. He would be able to get some regular game time under his belt at WBA and help their push for promotion under James Morrison.

Recent findings suggest that furlong, who is from Luton, knows the club inside out already and is a solid operator in the EFL. He knows what it takes to get out of the second tier and would be a useful character to have in and around the dressing room.

Sources indicate that prior to his switch to the Baggies, he rose up the ranks at QPR and played 72 times for their first-team in his early career. He also had spells away from the Hoops at Northampton Town, Cambridge United and Swindon Town to get some experience under his belt.

West Brom have been impressive this season but they lack depth. If Pereira got injured, WBA wouldn’t have anyone to play on the right hand side of their backline and would probably have to put Callum Styles there which wouldn’t be ideal.

Recent findings suggest that therefore, they need to consider a swoop for Furlong and it wouldn’t be a surprise to see Ipswich Town sanction a deal, either permanently or on loan. He is surplus to requirements with the Tractor Boys and should seek an exit.

#38395. Chelsea’s feisty friendly ends in penalty shoot-out confusion
